description_full: Generac Holdings Inc. designs, manufactures, and distributes energy technology products and solutions worldwide. The company offers residential automatic standby generators, automatic transfer switch, air-cooled engine home standby generators, and liquid-cooled engine generators; Mobile Link, a remote monitoring system for home standby generators; propane tank monitoring solution; and smart home solutions, such as smart thermostats and a suite of home monitoring products. It also provides smart home energy management devices and sensors for heating and cooling system; smart doorbell cameras; and portable and inverter generators; multiple portable battery solutions; manual transfer switches; outdoor power equipment, including trimmers, field and brush mowers, log splitters, stump grinders, chipper shredders, lawn and leaf vacuums, and pressure washers and water pumps; and home energy storage systems. In addition, the company offers commercial and industrial products comprising cleaner-burning natural gas fueled generators; mega-watt diesel generators; light-commercial standby generators and related transfer switches; stationary generators; single-engine industrial generators; industrial standby generators; industrial transfer switches; light towers, mobile generators, commercial mobile pumps, heaters, and dust-suppression equipment; mobile energy storage systems; battery energy storage system and related inverter products; and aftermarket service parts and product accessories. Further, it provides microgrid; and software-as-a-service contracts. The company distributes its products through independent residential dealers and contractors, industrial distributors and dealers, national and regional retailers, e-commerce partners, electrical/HVAC/solar wholesalers, solar installers, catalogs, equipment rental companies, and other equipment distributors; and directly to end users. Generac Holdings Inc. was founded in 1959 and is based in Waukesha, Wisconsin.

financial_summary: Generac Holdlings Inc. is a large-cap industrials business with a $11.3B market cap on $4.2B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -3% over the past three years and +12% annually across the full decade, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome.
Returns on capital run at 11% against a 10% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically, with gross margins sitting at 36%.

The business throws off $268M in free cash flow — roughly 6 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.75× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 1.9× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 4.1×.
Shareholder yield is only 1.3%, a thin return of capital, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome.

Tariff and trade-policy exposure — industrial exporters sit squarely in the crosshairs of protectionist policy, and retaliatory tariffs can close markets without warning.

sect: Its 7% operating margin is roughly in line with the Industrials median (9%).

mkt: The shares are in a strong uptrend, up 39% over the past year excluding the latest month, though it has pulled back 11% over the last three months.

val: The price sits above its DCF fair value of $184 (margin of safety -4%), so there is no valuation cushion.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 50%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $76.58 to $408 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks expensive against Industrials peers: P/E 37.6 vs 24.1, EV/EBITDA 20.0 vs 13.4 and P/FCF 42.0 vs 22.9 (sector median).
Against its own history it is dear: the EBIT multiple sits 139% above its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of 2.4% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 2.3% (vs the 8% bar).
The 18 covering analysts target $288 on average, 51% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 11% earns above the cost of capital of 10.4%, but the 1pp spread is short of the 7pp moat bar; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.41).
It runs a 36% gross margin and converts 6% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: cash conversion of 2.75x.
ROE of 6% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (2.1x equity multiplier).
It spends 5.8% of revenue on R&D and 1.2% on stock compensation.
hlth: Leverage is moderate at 1.9x net debt to EBITDA ($341.4M of cash against $1.3B of debt), above the 1.5x gate, with interest covered 4.1x.
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 4.3, in the safe zone).
Working capital ties up about 166 days of sales, a drag on cash generation.
growth: Revenue has compounded at -2.7% over 3 years, 11.1% over 5 years and 12.3% over 10 years, so growth is decelerating, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 18%).
At current returns, reinvesting 95% of profits supports about 10.9% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
Free cash flow has compounded -8.8% a year over five years, short of the 5% durability bar.
Forward indicators: a book-to-bill of 1.01, a backlog worth 4% of annual revenue and deferred revenue up 21%.
Capex roughly matches depreciation (0.9x, 4.0% of sales), a maintenance pace.
Its Rule of 40 score is 16, below the 40 that marks a healthy growth business.
own: Insiders own a modest 1.7%, and institutions hold 94%.
Insiders have only sold over the past year (19 sales, net $2.6M sold).
Shareholder yield is a modest 1.3% (1.3% in buybacks).
The share count has shrunk 1.2% a year over five years, steadily raising each holder's stake.
people: With about 9,400 employees, each generates about $448K of revenue, 1.2x the Industrials median, and revenue has grown 12.7% a year across its filed history.
That works out to $29K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $1.8M (4x revenue per employee), and compensation governance scores poorly (8/10, lower is better).
